report.summary: Reviewed the supplied three-file packet (lib/evidence-bundle.ts, app/guest-lab/evidence-viewer.ts, proofbeforepay-delivery SKILL.md) against the Cycle 22 supplemental plan. The plan itself (origin-issued Ed25519 receipt over the canonical bundle SHA-256, pinned SPKI, fail-closed signing config, wrong-key/tamper/digest tests) is consistent with the product boundaries: it keeps judgement, backend execution, human acceptance and payment unproven, and makes no third-party timestamp claim. One current defect is reachable and conflicts with the plan's fail-closed requirement: the offline viewer treats any internally consistent bundle as an acceptable result and never checks for an origin-issued receipt, so a stripped or substituted unsigned/re-signed-by-another-key file still produces a 'ready' state with 'Internally consistent'. That gives the UI no fail-closed path, and the plan's 'invalid/foreign signature, no silent removal/unsigned fallback' rule has no enforcement point. Design suggestions (not findings): add a receipt field (schema, keyId, issuer=mainSiteURL, issuedAt, optional digest, signature) re-verified against the pinned SPKI before 'ready'; keep the legacy unsigned result truthfully labelled ('unsigned, authenticity unproven'), and make it independently verifiable offline for old packets only. Add explicit receipt checks in the viewer gate list. Key-rotation should allow multiple pinned keyIds with an explicit retired-key policy, or old receipts become unverifiable. Say plainly that the pinned key makes the origin the trust anchor, not a third-party timestamp, and that a compromised or leaked main-app secret defeats the guarantee.

findings.title: Viewer reports 'Internally consistent' ready state without any origin-receipt check, so a stripped or foreign-signed file is not treated as fail-closed
findings.evidence: Line 192 renders the verdict from `state.verification.consistency` only, which comes from verifyEvidenceBundle. That function (lib/evidence-bundle.ts line 109) hardcodes `authenticity:"not-proven"` and has no signature input or check; lines 132-133 say 'There is no trusted signature or external anchor' and 'does not prove issuance'. The viewer's state machine (state.phase==='ready') never distinguishes a bundle that carries a valid origin receipt from one with a missing, tampered or foreign signature. Line 61 advertises v1/v2 support with no receipt, and line 140 shows legacy files as normal. The proposed receipt verifier therefore has no existing enforcement point in the current flow, and the plan's 'invalid/foreign signature is an invalid receipt, no silent removal or unsigned fallback' cannot hold for this viewer without a new check path.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): export a v2 bundle, remove any receipt, or re-sign it with an attacker key and re-run the same offline verify; verifyEvidenceBundle returns consistency 'consistent' (lines 112-118 and the check chain) and the viewer reaches line 191-192 showing the 'Internally consistent' verdict with no distinction from an official export. A buyer cannot tell from the UI that issuance is unproven.
findings.suggestion: Add a gated unsigned-vs-signed state: when `verification.receipt` is absent, render an explicit 'unsigned export, issuance unproven' label separate from 'Internally consistent' (and have legacy v1 continue to do so). When a receipt is present but its signature/digest/keyId/issuer fails against the pinned SPKI, render a distinct 'invalid receipt' verdict. Never fall back to the unsigned verdict for a failed signature. Render the 'Internally consistent' verdict only in the signed-and-verified case. Add viewer/receipt tests for missing receipt, wrong pinned key and tampered digest.

limitations: Read-only design review of a three-file packet; no files were modified and no commands, tests, typecheck, build or runtime checks were run.

The proposed source verifier, receipt schema, main-app signing code, Lab/repo public-key publication and test files are not in the packet, so their correctness and the reachability of signing-config fail-closed behavior cannot be assessed.
Only defects reachable in the current supplied code are reported; the absence of receipt verification elsewhere is treated as design guidance in the summary, not a finding outside the cited files.
SKILL.md was reviewed only as project guidance; it contains no runtime logic.
Trust-scope, key-rotation and compromised-secret limits are critique items for the design, not current-code findings.
The claim 'private PKCS8 only in existingSites main appsecret' cannot be verified here; no environment, secrets or app config were inspected.
